subtopic: KV Cache / Read-write pattern in prefill vs decode
learningObjective: Distinguish the KV cache read/write pattern in prefill vs decode and characterize the resulting HBM traffic per token.
stem: Consider a decoder-only transformer running (a) prefill on an input of length P, then (b) autoregressive decode for T new tokens. For a single attention layer with H_kv KV heads and head dim d, which characterization of KV cache HBM traffic is correct?

options.text: Prefill writes P tokens' KV once (O(P * H_kv * d)) and reads nothing; decode reads the growing cache once per step but does not write, so total KV bandwidth is O(P * H_kv * d + T * (P+T) * H_kv * d / 2) roughly.

Prefill and decode both write and read the entire KV cache every step: prefill because each token attends to all previous tokens, and decode because each step re-verifies previously written entries. Total KV bandwidth is O((P+T)^2 * H_kv * d).

KV cache is never touched in decode; decode only recomputes K and V from the current token and multiplies by all previous Q vectors that are re-read from HBM. Total KV bandwidth is therefore O(T * H_kv * d).

Prefill writes each of the P tokens' KV once and reads the growing cache for the causal attention (roughly O(P^2 * H_kv * d) reads inside a FlashAttention-style kernel this collapses to O(P^2 d / M) HBM). Decode writes exactly 1 new KV entry per step and reads the entire current cache (P + t) each step, giving read traffic Σ_{t=1..T} (P+t) * H_kv * d ≈ O(T*(P+T) * H_kv * d).

explanation: Prefill processes all P tokens in one attention call: it writes each token's K, V once (O(P*H_kv*d)) and computes causal attention which conceptually reads all pairs; with FlashAttention this HBM cost collapses. Decode is autoregressive: at step t (with cache length P + t − 1), the model writes one new K, V (O(H_kv * d)) and reads the entire cache (P + t) once. Summed over T steps, decode reads Σ_{t=1..T} (P + t) * H_kv * d ≈ T * (P + T/2) * H_kv * d.

optionExplanations.D: Correct: standard KV cache access pattern.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: prefill also reads the growing cache internally (attention over previously written tokens), and decode does write one entry per step.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no rewrite; each cache entry is written exactly once when the token is processed.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: decode reads KV cache, not previous Q vectors; Q is recomputed each step from the current token.

assumptions: Standard causal decoder attention (each token attends to all earlier positions including itself).
KV cache is a monotonically growing tensor; entries are written once and never overwritten (except on preemption).
nonImplications: Does not imply that PagedAttention changes the total bytes read, only the memory layout.
Does not imply that MQA/GQA changes this pattern qualitatively — it only scales H_kv.

distractorRationales.A: Denies prefill reads and decode writes.
